pages.text: "I don't like greens!" Yuki pushed the bowl of green vegetables to the table's edge, leaving one side empty. Yuki picked only rice and grilled fish.
"Grandma, I'm climbing to the mountain top today!" Yuki jumped off the porch. Grandma quietly looked at the pushed-away green bowl.
Halfway along the path, Yuki's legs grew heavy. Yuki sat on a rock. "I'm not even halfway there..." Brown dog Momo was ahead; Grandma followed with a basket.
Grandma sat beside Yuki and pointed uphill. "Let's rest, then gather greens. That slope is all green." Yuki looked up.
The slope really was green with mugwort, shepherd's purse, and bracken shoots. "Wow..." Yuki's mouth opened wide. The basket filled with green.
Grandma offered it to Yuki. "The green on our table came from here. It's strength from the mountain." Yuki pressed their nose to the leaves and sniffed.
At dinner, the green bowl returned. Yuki took a chopstickful. "...Oh? It tastes nutty! A Bite of Greens—Yum!" Yuki took another bite.
After the greens, Yuki's legs felt light. Yuki hopped around the porch, with Momo bouncing behind.
The next morning, Yuki adjusted the scarf knot before an empty bowl. "One, a green bite! Two, a white bite! Three, bites of everything!" Today, Yuki would reach the top.
At the top, Grandma hugged Yuki's shoulders. "You didn't rest once!" Eating greens gave Yuki strength to climb all the way. Looking down the mountain, Yuki smiled. "A Bite of Greens—Yum!"
